en.title: Pronouncing the Clitic Mi-e
en.summary: Learn how two words join into one quick sound when you pronounce mi-e in Romanian.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: In Romanian, two short words often melt together. The unit (mi-e) /mje/ sounds like one fast beat. You hear an m sound, then a quick glide, and an open vowel. Listen to (mi-e frig) /mje frig/, which means I am cold.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start with your lips closed for the first sound. Open your mouth quickly into the glide. Do not pause between the letters. Push your voice out in one single breath. Your tone stays smooth and fast. Say the whole unit quickly before you add (frig) /frig/.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: The hyphen shows that two words join together. You see two words, but you read one syllable. The first vowel becomes a quick glide like the 'y' in 'yes'. The second vowel takes the main energy. Whenever you read (mi-e) /mje/, never separate the parts.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make two separate beats. Never say two slow vowels with a pause. A small break between the letters sounds unnatural. Another mistake is dropping the first vowel completely. Keep both sounds alive in your mouth. Squeeze them together into one quick burst of air.
